sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
வெண்ணை வழிந்தோடக் கண்டேன் நங்கநல்லூரிலே
கண்ணை குளிரச்செய்யும் வாயுகுமரன் திரு உருவினிலே
sections.translit:
veNNai vazhindhOdak kaNdEn nanganallUrilE
kaNNai kuLiraccheyyum vAyukumaran thiru uruvinilE
sections.en: I saw butter flowing down the streets of Nanganallur, adorning the divine body of the wind god’s son, Hanuman.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
உயர்ந்து நின்றாய் உன் திரு வினையாலே நானோ
அயர்ந்து நின்றேன் நின் கோலவெழில் தண்மையாலே
sections.translit:
uyarndhu nindRAy un thiru vinaiyAlE nAnO
ayarndhu nindREn nin kOlavezhil thaNmaiyAlE
sections.en: You stand tall by the greatness you’ve achieved. I am awestruck by your beautiful form.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கடலில் கல்லெறிந்து அப்புறம் தாண்டியவர் உண்டோ
உடலில் தீப்பொறி தாங்கி ஊரை அழித்தவர் உண்டோ
அருவினை ஆற்றிவிட்டு இலங்கை சபை இலங்கினாற்போல்
உருவினை கொண்ட ஐயனே எம் இருவினை களைதலும் பெரும் பணியோ
sections.translit:
kadalil kalleRindhu appuRam thANdiyavar uNdO
udalil thIppoRi thAngi Urai azhitthavar uNdO
aruvinai AtRivittu ilangai sabhai ilanginARpOl
uruvinai koNda aiyanE em iruvinai kaLaidhalum perum paNiyO
sections.en: Is there anyone else who threw stones, and by that act alone, crossed an ocean? Is there anyone else who lit a whole city in flames by carrying a few sparks on their body? After completing mission impossible, you appear tall on a pedestal as though you were in Ravana’s court. For someone as accomplished as you, is it too big a task for you to absolve us of our past and present sins?

notes:
This song was composed after a visit to the Nanganallur Anchaneyar temple one evening, right after the arrival of the author in Chennai from Mumbai. It was impressive to see the sheer radiance of the tall Hanuman undergoing a வெண்ணை காப்பு (veNNai kAppu) on that day. No words can adequately describe the elegance of the son of Lord Vayu in granite coated with softening butter. The author was stunned by the height of the idol and was reminded of the story of Hanuman, who was denied a seat in Ravana’s court and twirled his boundless tail to make his own seat equal in height to the throne of the pompous king.
The author is aware that Valmiki Ramayana or the later versions of Ramayana do not contain this episode of Hanuman seating himself at a height equal to Ravana’s throne. This is folklore popular in several regions of India.
Hanuman was treated harshly in Ravana’s court despite all of the soft sermons he delivered to the king, urging him to follow the path of dharma and not invite the wrath of Lord Rama. Ravana ordered his guards to set fire to Hanuman’s tail as punishment for destroying the Ashoka forest and killing several soldiers. Hanuman used his tail to fan the flames and set Lanka on fire. The charanam line 2 describes the improbable mission accomplished by Hanuman.
